sentences: Do your stools look oily or greasy?
Then your pancreas may not be making enough digestive enzymes, called Exocrine Pancreatic Insufficiency, and you'd test for that with Stool Elastase and treat it with high-dose enzymes.
If too much of your bile is reaching your colon and giving you diarrhea (Bile Acid Diarrhea), Brown has you tested with SeHCAT and put on bile binders.

haiku: The paragraph is built as a diagnostic menu in which each condition gets the same sequence of symptom, name, test and treatment, so the rhythm is even and the two halves mirror each other. The voice is an instructive second person, which reads like a generic health explainer more than a single writer's argument.
sonnet: The paragraph is two parallel blocks, each running symptom, then condition name, then test, then treatment, with the same sentence shapes and a similar length. That even, checklist-like rhythm and the absence of any personal stance or aside make it feel assembled rather than spoken. It does not read as strongly machine-made, though, since the voice is brisk and the content is compressed.
